verdict.reasoning: Headache is left-sided, throbbing, since mid-day and worse with movement: “terrible headache since mid-day… on the left side… throbbing… if I lean forward, or like move my head or neck, yeah, headache gets worse.”

Visual aura described with zig-zag lines and blurred vision in both eyes: “I noticed some zig-zag lines in my vision a few minutes before the headache started… my vision has been blurry as well… Both eyes, OK.”
Photophobia, nausea, and two episodes of vomiting are documented: “the light's really hurting my eyes… you mentioned that you felt quite nauseous. Have you vomited at all?… I vomited twice.”

Prior similar headache a few weeks ago lasting a couple of days, needing rest, painkillers, and causing missed work: “I did have a similar headache a few weeks ago… Couple of days… I had to take painkillers, and had to go go to bed and rest… couple days off work, and I work in the fashion industry.”
Patient denies prior migraine diagnosis: “has anyone told you you've had migraines in the past? Patient: No.”
Family history includes mother with migraines and underactive thyroid: “My mum, my mum has, has migraines… My mom has an underactive thyroid as well.”
Microgynon taken for contraception: “Um I take the pill, Microgynon… it's for contraception.”
Works in fashion industry with high job stress: “I work in the fashion industry… it's really stressful, actually… managers like putting a lot of pressure on me.”
Lives alone and does not exercise: “I live on my own… Do you do much in the way of exercise? Patient: No.”
Non-smoker and does not drink alcohol: “Do you smoke at all? and do you drink much in the way of alcohol? Patient: No. No.”

Migraine with aura is inferred from unilateral throbbing headache, visual aura, photophobia, nausea, and vomiting, and the doctor labels it migraine: “I noticed some zig-zag lines… blurry… headache on one side, throbbing nature, the nausea, vomiting, sensitivity to bright lights… I wonder whether you may, uh may have a migraine.”

This is the second migraine this month with no focal neurological deficits and no red flags: “this is the second migraine you've had in the space of a month” and neurologic screen negative: “Any problems with your speech… arms and legs… balance…? Patient: No… I'm reassured that you don't have anything more serious, such as meningitis, or indeed Brain cancer.”

Health anxiety about brain tumor is clear: “I've read… it could be a sign of brain cancer… My friend's mum… died of a brain tumor. So, it's really concerning me actually… I was so worried that I had cancer.”

Work-related stress documented: “you work in the fashion industry… is your job quite stressful at the moment? Patient: Yeah it's really stressful, actually… managers like putting a lot of pressure on me.”
Analgesia options explicitly listed: “some strong painkillers would be advisable. So, think about Paracetamol, or even Co-codamol… some anti-inflammatories, such as Ibuprofen and Naproxen.”
Headache diary advised: “I think keeping a headache diary would be quite important, uh to see exactly what's triggering these headaches.”

Prophylactic medications if headaches become persistent: “if your headaches were to become more persistent, then we could maybe think about giving you some medications that will stop your headaches from happening in the first place, something prophylactic medicines.”

Safety net advice matches: “if your symptoms aren't getting better next two three days, or indeed they're getting worse… if your headache's getting worse, not responding to medications… Or your um neck pain is getting worse, or you develop any weakness in your arms and legs, or your vision, then I want you to come back and see me straight away.”

Reassurance about low concern for meningitis or brain cancer: “I'm reassured that you don't have anything more serious, such as meningitis, or indeed Brain cancer, I know that was a big worry of yours initially.”
Follow-up next week is suggested: “then we could have a discussion next time I see you next week, perhaps.”
